agentWallReview.evidence: Native development app AX showed full-screen RAM-weighted tiles for terminal Codex and Devin sessions. Fresh provider hooks changed Devin from Working to Stopped and identified the correct terminal Codex tile with its latest request. Both temporary tiles disappeared when their processes exited. Detached shared Codex hosts remained off the wall.

Multiple conversations in one host can share a tile.

contract.purpose: Explain why a Mac feels slow and provide one safe, evidence-backed next step.
contract.canonicalPurpose: PerformanceDaddy helps Mac users investigate slowdowns, understand active workloads, find regressions against known-good evidence and optimize repeatable workflows through bounded native measurement and comparable verification.
contract.audience: Mac users, especially developers, who do not want to interpret raw system metrics.
contract.job: Turn a slowdown captured now into a trustworthy cause and safe next action.
contract.thesis: A calm plain-language verdict should lead; technical evidence should earn confidence through progressive disclosure.
contract.system: Owner-approved Daddy-series black canvas, mint actions, quiet typography, flat evidence tables, progressive disclosure and restrained doodle artwork; diagnosis retains NOW, WHY and NEXT narrative bands.
contract.signature: A calm black-and-mint evidence workspace turns live workload data into an inspectable next action.
contract.risk: Dense evidence can become visually noisy, so secondary detail stays behind inspectors and disclosures while primary measurements remain sortable.

detector.note: The web-oriented detector does not support Swift; native source and live AX review were used instead.

fanInvestigationReview.audience: Mac users hearing fan noise, especially developers with active builds and background workloads.
fanInvestigationReview.job: Explain possible measured heat contributors without substituting CPU or thermal state for a fan-speed reading.
fanInvestigationReview.system: Existing black canvas, mint actions, pale-mint secondary text, amber confidence, system typography and 7pt controls. Layout and information hierarchy await owner selection.

directions.thesis: Explanation first, with NOW / WHY / NEXT narrative bands.
directions.layout: Large verdict and a single vertically sequenced investigation.
directions.typography: 34pt leading verdict, 20pt band titles, quiet evidence rows.
directions.interaction: Progressive evidence disclosure and one equal-length recapture action.
directions.signature: User-reported fan incident becomes a measured explanation and discriminating next check.
directions.risk: Experts may need to expand the detail.

directions.layout: Summary strip, resource readings and a wide CPU timeline with contributor detail.
directions.typography: Short large title, compact verdict, numeric resource readings.
directions.interaction: Inspect the measured time window and repeat a comparable capture.
directions.signature: Activity settling is visible without implying measured fan settling.
directions.risk: A chart may imply causal timing; fan/GPU non-measurement stays explicit.

directions.thesis: Measured coverage and ranked explanations share the screen.
directions.layout: Dense evidence table and process contributors beside a numbered investigation rail.
directions.typography: Resource labels and aligned numerical rows, smaller explanatory paragraphs.
directions.interaction: Inspect resource coverage and process evidence before recapture.
directions.signature: Unknown sensor coverage is as visible as available measurements.
directions.risk: More demanding for casual users; plain-language investigation stays adjacent.
